title: Winter Bungeoppang
description:
On the way home, a bungeoppang cart on the corner — fish-shaped pastries filled with red bean.
Three for a thousand won. The paper bag warms your hands as you blow on them.

These days there's even an app that maps where they're being sold.
— Korea's winter streets smell different.

choices.text: Bungeoppang plus free fish-cake broth — thaw out the cold
choices.result_text:
Head first or tail first — that silly little dilemma felt good.
The fish-cake broth is free. You cupped the paper cup in both hands.

A thousand won of warmth. Gangnam's far, but this alley was warm tonight.

choices.text: Buy a bag and eat alone in my room
choices.result_text:
Ate the cooled bungeoppang in your goshiwon room.
Soggy, but the sweetness held.

That there's comfort even in bungeoppang eaten alone — that's something you learned in Seoul.

title: Comfort at the Bunsik Shop
description:
On a low day, a bunsik (snack) shop.
Tteokbokki, sundae, fried things, and gimmari.

For the moment you're dipping fried squid into the spicy sauce,
Even your bank balance and Gangnam slip your mind.

choices.text: Go big — tteokbokki with sundae and fritters
choices.result_text:
Spicy enough to make your nose run, spicy enough to keep eating.
Dunked the fritters deep in the tteokbokki sauce. Whoever invented that combo is a genius.

Nine thousand won buys no better comfort. Korea's soul food.

choices.text: Just one order of plain tteokbokki
choices.result_text:
A solo order felt a little sheepish, but the lady piled on extra rice cakes.
"Eat up, young man."
That one line warmed you more than the tteokbokki did.

title: Malatang and Tanghulu
description:
Lately the streets are all malatang and tanghulu.
You pick your own ingredients into a bowl and choose your spice level.

They came from China but got Koreanized into a craze.
Trends arrive fast and leave fast — that, too, is Korea.

choices.result_text:
Tried spice level 2 and set my mouth on fire.
The candied tanghulu barely put it out. Spicy then sweet, a chaotic combo.

Followed the trend once. Next month it'll be something else, sure.

choices.text: Skip the trend, just hit Gimbap Heaven
choices.result_text:
Ended up at the familiar Gimbap Heaven. Ramyeon and a roll of gimbap.

Trends pass fast, but the bunsik-shop ramyeon has been in the same spot for ten years.
There's a steadiness in things that don't change.

title: Facing the Delivery App
description:
After overtime, an empty goshiwon room.
You open the delivery app. Minimum order 15,000, delivery fee 3,500.

You add to cart, remove, add again.
Between 4.8 stars and 4.6, you deliberate for ages.

choices.text: Forget it, order it — I earned it today
choices.result_text:
Chicken at the door thirty minutes later.
Eating alone, you still tap 'leave it at the door' — that's the Korean way.

The fee stings, but in front of a warm meal it's forgotten.
A 19,000-won reward to yourself for surviving the day.

choices.text: The fee feels wasteful — head to the convenience store
choices.result_text:
Closed the app in the end. A convenience-store lunchbox and cup ramyeon.

Saving the 3,500-won fee felt satisfying and a little sad at once.
These small calculations add up to Gangnam, you told yourself.

title: All-You-Can-Eat Meat
description:
Fifteen thousand won a head, all-you-can-eat barbecue.
Samgyeopsal sizzles on the grill.

The Korean instinct to 'get your money's worth' kicks in.
Lettuce, meat, garlic, ssamjang — a full wrap in one bite.

choices.text: Eat past your money's worth — to the stomach's limit
choices.result_text:
Fifth plate. You know it's too much, and reach for one more piece.

Your belly's about to burst, your heart's content.
The fullness of 'eating my fill' for once. There have to be days like this too.

choices.text: Eat a reasonable amount and leave early
choices.result_text:
Stopped at two plates. A little wistful about the 'value,' but your stomach was at ease.

Restraint in front of a buffet is a skill too.
Overeating and overreaching — you're the one who pays for both the next day.
